# Part 1: Template, VFD Pump Control Narrative

**Rule for authors:** Do not type tag ranges, setpoints, or delay times into this document. Refer to the tag, and the I/O list and alarm database stay the single source of truth. Values appear only if they are logic constants not held in those sheets, and then they are marked `[param]`. Delete guidance text in *italics* when filling in.

## 2. Equipment and Signals

# Part 2: Filled Example, CN-P-1102

**CN-P-1102: Mix Tank to Hold Tank Transfer Pump**
Rev: A (draft) Date: 2026-10-18 Author: [ ] Reviewer: [ ] P&ID ref: [ ] Source rev of I/O list / alarm DB: [ ]

## 1. Purpose
P-1102 transfers product from mix tank T-110 to hold tank T-120. It is variable speed (VFD), started and stopped by the batch system in Auto, with speed set by the batch system.

## 2. Equipment and Signals

| Role | Tag | Type | Used in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run command | P-1102 (run cmd) | DO / fieldbus | 6, 7 |
| Run feedback | P-1102 (run fb) | DI / fieldbus | 6, 9 |
| VFD fault | P-1102 (VFD fault) | DI / fieldbus | 5, 9 |
| Speed reference | SIC-1102 (SP/OUT) | Fieldbus/AO | 8 |
| Speed feedback | SI-1102 | Fieldbus/AI | 9 |
| Suction dry-run protection | LSL-110 | DI | 4, 5 |
| Discharge pressure | PT-1102 | AI | 5, 9 |
| Receiving tank high level | LSH-120 | DI | 4, 5 |

*Tag names above follow the narrative; use the exact names from the I/O list. Add motor temperature, local E-stop, or HOA rows if they exist in the I/O list.*

## 3. Modes
| Mode | Start/stop | Speed | Interlocks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto | Batch system | Batch system reference | Active |
| Manual | Operator via HMI | Operator entry on HMI | Active |
| Out of service | None | None | Trips only |

On controller restart the pump is in Manual and stopped. Changing mode while running does not stop the pump. When switching Auto to Manual, the current speed is held as the manual setpoint (bumpless). Switching Manual to Auto is accepted only if the batch system is providing a valid reference.

## 4. Start Permissives
| # | Condition | Source | Bad-quality behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | T-110 level adequate (LSL-110 not in low state) | LSL-110 | Treat as not satisfied |
| P2 | T-120 not full (LSH-120 not in high state) | LSH-120 | Treat as not satisfied |
| P3 | No VFD fault present | VFD fault | Treat as fault |
| P4 | No latched trip active (Section 5) | internal | n/a |
| P5 | Mode is Auto or Manual (not Out of service) | internal | n/a |
| P6 | In Auto: valid speed reference received | batch reference | Treat as not satisfied |

The HMI displays the first unsatisfied permissive as "Not ready: [text]".

## 5. Run Interlocks (Stop/Trip)
| # | Condition | Tag | Delay | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | T-110 low level (dry-run protection) | LSL-110 | Debounce `[param]` | Trip stop | Operator reset once LSL-110 clear |
| I2 | T-120 high level | LSH-120 | Debounce `[param]` | Normal stop (ramp down) | Auto-clear when LSH-120 clears; batch system must re-command start |
| I3 | Discharge pressure high-high | PT-1102 | Per alarm DB | Trip stop | Operator reset after pressure below limit |
| I4 | Low discharge pressure while running (loss of prime / line break), enabled after run-up delay `[param]` | PT-1102 | Per alarm DB | Trip stop | Operator reset |
| I5 | VFD fault | VFD fault | None | Trip stop | Operator reset after VFD fault clears |
| I6 | Run feedback lost while commanded | run fb | `[param]` | Trip stop | Operator reset |
| I7 | PT-1102 or LSL-110 bad quality | respective tag | `[param]` | Trip stop | Auto-clear when quality returns; operator reset required |

I1, I3 to I7 are latched. A trip stop removes the run command immediately, and the VFD coasts or stops per its drive configuration.

## 6. Start Sequence
1. Start command received (batch system in Auto, operator in Manual) and all permissives satisfied.
2. Speed reference set to the clamped starting value (Section 8).
3. Run command issued to the VFD.
4. Run feedback must be received within `[param]` s; otherwise alarm "Failed to start" and trip (I6).
5. After run-up delay `[param]`, the low-pressure interlock I4 is enabled.
6. Status changes to Running.

## 7. Stop Sequence
- **Normal stop** (batch command, operator command, I2): ramp speed to minimum per the ramp parameter, then remove the run command. If run feedback does not drop within `[param]` s, raise "Failed to stop".
- **Trip stop** (I1, I3 to I7): run command removed immediately and trip latched with first-out indication.

## 8. Speed Control
- Auto: speed reference from the batch system. Manual: operator entry on HMI.
- Reference is clamped between minimum and maximum speed (engineering limits per I/O list).
- Ramp up and ramp down rates are `[param]`, set on the VFD or in the PLC. State which in Open Items.
- If the batch reference is bad quality or comms is lost while running in Auto: hold last good value for `[param]` s and alarm, then normal stop.

## 9. Fault Detection
| Fault | Alarm tag | Detection | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Failed to start | P-1102 FTS | No run fb within time | Trip |
| Failed to stop | P-1102 FTO | Run fb after stop | Alarm only |
| Speed deviation | SI-1102 dev | Feedback vs. reference outside band for `[param]` s | Alarm only |
| VFD fault | P-1102 VFD | VFD fault bit | Trip |
| Dry-run trip | LSL-110 trip | I1 | Trip |
| High discharge pressure | PT-1102 HH | I3 | Trip |
| Low discharge pressure | PT-1102 LL | I4 | Trip |

*Use exact alarm tag IDs from the alarm DB.*

## 10. Alarms
All alarm priorities, setpoints, and delays are in the alarm database. This narrative uses the alarms listed in Section 9 plus the reference-loss alarm in Section 8, plus any PT-1102 high/low pre-alarms that exist in the DB. Reviewers should confirm each alarm in the DB maps to a row here and the reverse.

## 11. Reset and Restart
- Latched trips (I1, I3 to I7) require an operator reset on the faceplate, and the initiating condition must be clear.
- No automatic restart after a trip or after controller or power restart. Pump comes up stopped in Manual.
- After a normal stop due to I2, the batch system must issue a new start.

## 12. HMI Requirements
- Faceplate: mode, status, run command, speed SP/PV, PT-1102 value, permissive and interlock status with first-out trip, reset button.
- Operator commands: start, stop, mode, manual speed, reset.
- Engineer-only: delay and ramp parameters, bypass if the site permits any (see Open Items).

## 13. Failure Modes of Instruments
| Signal | Failure behavior |
|---|---|
| LSL-110 | Wire break or bad quality reads as low (fail-safe); I1/I7 trips |
| LSH-120 | Wire break or bad quality reads as high; prevents start, normal stop if running |
| PT-1102 | Bad quality trips via I7 |
| Batch speed reference | See Section 8 |
| VFD comms | Loss treated as VFD fault (I5) |

## 14. Commissioning Checks
| Test | Expected |
|---|---|
| Force LSL-110 low with pump stopped, attempt start | Start blocked, "Not ready" text correct |
| Force LSL-110 low while running | Immediate trip, latched, reset required |
| Force LSH-120 high while running | Ramp-down stop; no latch |
| Simulate PT-1102 above HH limit | Trip, latched |
| Simulate PT-1102 low after run-up delay | Trip |
| Remove run feedback | Failed-to-start or run fb lost trip |
| Remove batch reference in Auto | Alarm, hold, then normal stop |
| Controller restart while running | Pump stopped, Manual mode, no auto restart |
| Verify each tag and alarm ID against I/O list and alarm DB | Match |

## 15. Open Items / Assumptions
1. Assumed no discharge valve is interlocked with this pump. Confirm on P&ID and add a permissive and interlock if one exists.
2. Confirm whether a local E-stop, HOA switch, or motor thermal input exists, and add to Sections 2 and 5.
3. Confirm whether ramps are set in the VFD or PLC.
4. Confirm that LSL-110 and LSH-120 are fail-safe wired (open on low or high condition) as assumed in Section 13.
5. Confirm whether the site allows interlock bypasses, and if so their authorization and logging.

---

**Notes on the template design**
- Permissives and interlocks are separate tables because they behave differently (start-only versus run-and-stop). Mixing them is a common source of logic errors.
- Every row names a tag but no value. That keeps the narrative from drifting out of sync with your spreadsheets. The one cross-check you may want to automate is Section 10 against the alarm DB.
- The `[param]` items (delays, ramps, timeouts) are the ones that are not in your spreadsheets today. If you collect them in a parameter sheet per module, the narrative can reference that too.
- I assumed the specific alarm tag names and the fail-safe behaviors in the example. Check them against your actual databases before issuing.
